Replace the inconsistent imported 19 July endpoint with 28 June. The raw source also contains 29 June Gregorian and July 18–19 Julian claims; these are not silently converted into a multi-week battle. The date review concerns the battle itself, not the later Swedish withdrawal/campaign.

note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 38, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Approve the exact one-day Fehrbellin battle after replacing the published 19 July end with 28 June 1675. GHI dates the battle to 28 June; ZMSBw describes a short battle between the Swedish army and the Elector of Brandenburg’s predominantly cavalry force. The CDB90 6000 Brandenburg personnel are not an infantry count. Its Swedish 6400 estimate has a +72 percent qualifier (upper bound 11008), whereas ZMSBw gives 7000 infantry and 4000 cavalry. ZMSBw’s roughly 4000 Swedish losses explicitly include deserters; they do not replace CDB90’s 2500 personnel battle casualties. Differences of estimates and categories are retained, not treated as proof of exact agreement. Both CDB90 strengths are initial totals without source reinforcements. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name PR ARMY): The force of Elector Frederick William, Derfflinger and Hesse-Homburg was predominantly cavalry with artillery, as ZMSBw explains. The original PR ARMY shorthand is retained in the quantity provenance; the local name avoids treating a later Prussian state as the literal participant. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name SW ARMY): ZMSBw identifies the Swedish army under Waldemar von Wrangel, with infantry and cavalry. The source’s force estimate differs from CDB90 and is not substituted.
